standard.title: Language reflects cultural practices, values and identity
standard.description: recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity, and that this impacts on non-verbal and spoken communication
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify connections between the target language and cultural practices using conceptual vocabulary (AC9LS4U04). They reflect on cross-cultural comparisons. They have not yet explored contact language influences on the target language, examined cultural stereotypes critically, or analysed modern language change.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity — including through contact language influences, cultural stereotypes, modern language change, and First Nations Australian cultural expressions.

nodes.label: Contact language influences and cultural stereotypes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how contact with other languages has influenced the target language vocabulary, and recognise that cultural stereotypes about target language communities are oversimplifications.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three target language words derived from contact or indigenous languages and explain their origin; identify at least one cultural stereotype and explain why it oversimplifies.
nodes.typical_width: Explore contact language contributions to the target language vocabulary; recognise that contact languages remain important for identity and heritage; become aware of cultural stereotypes that lead to generalisations; recognise shared linguistic history with related language families.
wider: Research a contact language that has influenced the target language — identify several loanwords and explain what they reveal about the relationship between the two communities
Examine a cultural stereotype about target language communities — find evidence that contradicts it and explain why the stereotype persists
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding contact language influence and the danger of stereotypes is foundational to authentic intercultural competence. Students with a single-community, stereotype-based model of target language culture cannot engage with genuine cultural diversity.

response_modes.reason: Stereotype identification and critique requires students to move from passive noticing to active analysis — identifying what a stereotype claims, finding contradicting evidence and explaining the mechanism by which stereotypes persist.

success_criteria: Identifies at least three target language words with contact language origins and explains each
Identifies at least one cultural stereotype and explains why it is an oversimplification

nodes.label: Modern language change and identity expression
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how modern influences shape target language change, and reflect on visible and invisible elements of identity expressed through language.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two modern influences on the target language and explain how each has changed the language; identify at least one visible and one invisible element of cultural identity.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate modern influences on the target language — digital culture, migration, pop culture; explore First Nations Australian cultural expressions through song, dance or artworks; reflect on culturally appropriate communication conventions; understand shared and distinct visible and invisible identity elements across cultures.
wider: Compare how digital and social media culture has changed the target language in two different target language communities
Explore how cultural expressions of First Nations Australians through song, dance or artworks compare with those of target language communities — identify similarities and differences in one aspect

response_modes.reason: Language change awareness develops through encountering varied change drivers — digital culture, migration, pop culture, regional contact. Each reveals a different mechanism by which language evolves.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Modern language change — particularly digital and social media vocabulary — connects target language learning to students' everyday language experience, making the target language feel current and alive rather than only historical.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two modern influences on the target language and explains how each has changed it
Identifies at least one visible and one invisible element of cultural identity and explains how each is expressed through language
